title: Noor and the Echo
premise: Kestrel Montrose, an insurance investigator who documents the slow collapse of the forgotten colony on Meridian-9, discovers a name on a ship's manifest that shouldn't exist — Noor, listed as crew of a vessel that never launched. The trail leads her to a hidden cryo-fleet where two factions, the colony's original founders and the corporate board that abandoned them, each hold half the sleepers hostage to a truce about to expire. Kestrel falls for Noor's brother Idris, the fleet's reluctant archivist, even as she realizes justice for Meridian-9 can't come from any court. In the end she wakes both halves at once, forcing the factions to share one fragile future or destroy it together.
about_author: Elodie Eriksen is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade writing loss reports before turning them into fiction. She lives in Tromsø, where the long polar nights taught her that some stories only surface in the dark.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Ruin
chapters.summary: Kestrel files her 400th report on Meridian-9's dying infrastructure, cataloging a collapsed water reclaimer no one will pay out on. Her POV establishes her dry, forensic detachment and private grief over the colony everyone forgot. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism, cracked when she notices an anomaly in an old shipping manifest.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Kestrel traces the ghost vessel Halcyon Step and finds its launch records scrubbed from every registry except one: a passenger named Noor Vashti, timestamped after the ship was decommissioned. Following the paper trail off-world, she is detained by fleet security who seem less surprised than alarmed. Beat: curiosity hardening into obsession; first hint she's being watched.

chapters.title: The Sleeping Half
chapters.summary: Aboard the cryo-fleet Concordance, Kestrel meets Idris Vashti, who maintains the archives of ten thousand sleepers frozen during the evacuation he believes was a rescue. He doesn't know his sister Noor woke early and vanished into the fleet's sealed decks. Beat: wary attraction between two people who both keep records of things gone wrong.

chapters.title: Noor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Idris POV: through Noor's hidden journal entries embedded in the archive, we learn she discovered the founders rigged the truce — when it expires, their half wakes and the corporate sleepers are quietly vented. Idris must choose between loyalty to the founders who raised him and his sister's evidence. Beat: betrayal, and the first taste of power's corruption.

chapters.title: Terms of the Truce
chapters.summary: Kestrel infiltrates a founder council session using her insurance credentials as cover, witnessing Director Sable Voss calmly justify the purge as 'actuarial necessity.' She recognizes her own profession's language weaponized. Caught leaving, she's spared only because Voss wants a witness — a warning to others. Beat: fear fused with fury; love against duty begins pulling at her.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Idris and Kestrel become lovers in the archive stacks, trading secrets like contraband. Together they find Noor alive, hiding among maintenance levels, half-feral from years alone with the truth. But Noor doesn't trust Kestrel — an investigator, a corporate tool. Beat: tenderness shadowed by suspicion; the trio forms anyway, bound by shared evidence.

chapters.title: The Venting Schedule
chapters.summary: Noor reveals the full plan: the countdown is real, days remain, and the corporate faction has its own counter-scheme — waking first by force, which would kill the founders' sleepers in the crossfire. Justice outside the law means sabotage, but targeting either side makes them murderers. Beat: moral vertigo; Kestrel proposes the impossible third option — wake everyone simultaneously.

chapters.title: Countdown on the Concordance
chapters.summary: Rising action: the three race through the fleet's guts to override the truce protocol while Voss's security hunts them. Idris is captured and offered his old life back if he surrenders the archive keys. He refuses. Beat: sacrifice and resolve; Kestrel must choose between saving Idris and reaching the master control.

chapters.title: Wake Everyone
chapters.summary: Climax: Kestrel triggers simultaneous revival of all ten thousand sleepers as Voss tries to vent the corporate bays; Noor physically holds the breach controls; Idris, escaping custody, broadcasts the founders' own ledger fleet-wide so every waking person sees the truth. Voss is arrested by the people she meant to cull. Beat: chaos, courage, love declared in the middle of catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Long Morning
chapters.summary: Resolution: ten thousand strangers wake to cold coffee and a reckoning. A provisional council forms with Noor, Idris, and Kestrel — the investigator, the archivist, the ghost — drafting justice no court ever planned. The fleet turns toward Meridian-9, not as a graveyard but a home worth rebuilding. Final beat: Kestrel writes one last report, filed under 'settled.'
